sections.title: UB discipline — where C++ punishes the unwary

blocks.label: traps and their fixes
blocks.py:
# TRAP 1: integer division floor toward NEGATIVE infinity
-7 // 2 == -4            # C++ gives -3! Know the difference
mid = lo + (hi - lo) // 2

# TRAP 2: no fixed-width overflow - ints are arbitrary precision
big = 10**30 * 10**30    # fine. Modulo discipline still used for speed.

# TRAP 3: shifting
1 << 31                  # perfectly legal - no sign-bit UB in Python

# TRAP 4: float equality
0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3         # False! use math.isclose for floats

blocks.text: Strict weak ordering — the silent killer

blocks.label: comparator contract
blocks.py:
# comparator contract becomes a KEY function (always well-ordered):
words.sort(key=lambda w: (len(w), w))   # length asc, ties alphabetical

# multi-key descending on one field:
items.sort(key=lambda p: (-p.score, p.id))

# functools.cmp_to_key exists for true comparators - avoid when possible.

blocks.md: Answers demanded modulo 10⁹+7 (prime) exist to fit in 64 bits while keeping numbers huge. Rules: add/subtract freely with %; MULTIPLY ONLY AFTER widening; division becomes modular inverse via Fermat: `a^(M−2)`.

blocks.label: the three tools
blocks.py:
MOD = 10**9 + 7

def modmul(a, b): return (a % MOD) * (b % MOD) % MOD

def modpow(base, exp):            # built-in: pow(base, exp, MOD)
    r = 1; base %= MOD
    while exp > 0:
        if exp & 1: r = r * base % MOD
        base = base * base % MOD
        exp >>= 1
    return r

def moddiv(a, b): return a * modpow(b, MOD - 2) % MOD   # Fermat inverse

blocks.title: Trace: modpow(3, 13, MOD) — consuming exponent bits

blocks.md: **Negative modulo trap:** `(a−b) % MOD` can print negative in C++. Canonical fix: `((a − b) % MOD + MOD) % MOD`.

items.q: MOD must be prime for Fermat inverse because…
options: a^(p−2) identity requires gcd(a,p)=1 guaranteed by primality
items.explain: Composite modulus needs extended-Euclid inverse instead.

items.q: Counting paths under grid mod 1e9+7: intermediate sums may reach…
items.explain: One multiply doubles digit count; one add doesn't. Widen exactly at multiplies.

items.title: Optimised Sieve + Complexity Defense
items.statement: Implement sieve to 10⁷ with bitset/vector<bool>; defend O(n log log n) using harmonic-style sum n/2+n/3+n/5+… and memory math (bytes used).
hints: Sum over primes p≤n of n/p = n·ln ln n.
vector<bool>: 1 bit per entry — say why byte-array variant trades speed/space.
Odd-only sieve halves memory — implement as extension.

items.title: Product of Primes in [L,R] mod M
items.statement: Compose segmented sieve + empty-product edge cases + modmul chain across the window.
hints: Zero primes in window → answer 1? Clarify statement semantics first.
Window scan multiplies through modmul only.

items.title: Modular Exponentiation (iterative, battle-safe)
items.statement: Compute (a^b) % M for b up to 10¹⁸; handle a=0, M=1, negative a normalization.
hints: Reduce a % M first including negatives: ((a%M)+M)%M.
Trace exponent bits on paper for b=13 before coding.

items.title: SPOJ EKO — Binary Search on Answer (preview)
items.statement: Max height H so that cutting trees yields ≥ M wood. Monotonic feasibility ⇒ binary search the ANSWER space, not an array.
hints: Feasible(H) is monotone: taller cut ⇒ less wood.
This pattern returns in Module 04 with Aggressive Cows & Book Allocation.

items.title: Comparator Contract Autopsy
items.statement: Given a broken `<=` comparator crashing sort on duplicates, prove violation, fix it, write the 3-rule strict-weak-ordering checklist from memory.
hints: Test suite MUST include equal elements — that's what detonates it.
Explain how libstdc++ descends out-of-bounds when contract breaks.

revisionCard: Read CONSTRAINTS first — they select the algorithm class
Preamble: sync off · tie null · '\n' not endl · ll by default
Overflow: widen BEFORE multiply (1LL*a*b) · mid = lo+(hi-lo)/2 · 1<<31 is UB
Comparator = strict weak ordering or sort corrupts memory; test with equal keys
Iterator invalidation: vector reallocates→all die; list/map/set never
Mod world: widen at multiplies only · ((a-b)%M+M)%M · inverse via a^(M-2) (prime M)

glossary.def: Mapping from input bound to affordable complexity (~10⁸ ops/sec heuristic).
Irreflexive, asymmetric, transitive comparison contract required by sort/set/map.
Rules determining which iterators/references survive container mutation.
b^(M−2) mod prime M playing the role of 1/b under mod arithmetic.
Σn style limits bounding TOTAL input across test cases.
Searching monotonic feasible/infeasible boundary over values instead of array positions.
Standard imposes no requirements — compiler may assume impossibility and misoptimize.
